Broadlea Primary School
Welcome to Broadlea Primary School
I am delighted to welcome you to Broadlea Primary School, where our values of Aspiration, Resilience and Kindness underpin everything we do as we support every child to be the best they can be.
It is a great privilege to lead a team of skilled and reflective staff who prioritise the needs of children at the centre of all they do. Our school is a place where every child is valued as an individual and everyone strives to achieve their very best in all they do.
We are committed to ensuring that pupils are ready for the next stage of education and our curriculum is carefully designed to motivate and excite our children whilst providing them with the knowledge, skills, vocabulary and inspiration they need to embrace their future. By supporting our children to develop resilience, curiosity, compassion, understanding and aspiration, we lay the building blocks to ensure they are ready for the next stage in their learning and beyond.
Our Learning Environment
We aim to provide a rich and varied curriculum through our extensive learning environment, including Forest School, our beautiful library, art room and extensive school grounds. In February 2024, our completely repurposed and extensive Early Years and Key Stage One learning environment was opened, creating a state-of-the-art provision where learning and play are truly irresistible. Building on the impact this refurbished environment had on learning, we have redecorated the remainder of school to create calm learning spaces using a therapeutic approach which we believe is essential.
Reading and Early Learning
Children begin to learn to read, write and spell using our chosen phonics programme, Little Wandle, as soon as they begin school. Our uncompromising ambition is for all children to become fluent and confident readers who learn to read so they can read to learn. Our phonics results are consistently strong, ensuring children have the foundational skills they need to succeed.
High-Quality Teaching for All
We are focused on embedding high-quality, inclusive teaching in every classroom, ensuring that all learners—especially our disadvantaged pupils and those with SEND—receive the support they need to thrive. We strive to be an inclusive school and are very proud of our children and staff: they are so supportive of one another and work hard every day to ensure that our school is a place where everyone feels valued and included.
Enrichment and Cultural Capital
At Broadlea, we encourage learning beyond the classroom, enhancing children's cultural capital through visiting places of interest, inviting visitors into school and utilising our beautiful local area. Our Forest School natural, tree-enclosed environment offers all learners, from Reception to Year 6, regular opportunities to achieve and develop confidence and self-esteem through hands-on learning experiences.
We are delighted to be a School Games Platinum school and to be working towards reaccreditation of our Arts Mark. Both accreditations recognise the range of clubs, activities and opportunities provided for our children.
Partnership with Families
To achieve our ambitions for every child, we believe that partnership and communication between home and school is essential. We work closely with our families to ensure the best outcomes for all children. Parents have high expectations for pupils' pastoral care and personal development, and we are committed to working together to achieve these. All classes have Class Dojo accounts set up to support communication between home and school and our Family Liaison Officer is available to provide additional support for families as needed.
At Broadlea, your child will be celebrated as an individual whilst joining a strong community of parents, children, staff and governors, whose joint aim is to provide the highest possible standard of education. I hope that this website will help you to find out about the life of our very special school. However, the best way to learn more is to come in and see us, look around the school, and see for yourself what we have to offer.
We very much look forward to meeting you.
Lynn Torrance - Headteacher

Broadlea Primary School
Puffins After-School Care
After-School Care runs from 3 - 5.30pm in the Key Stage 2 block accessed via the green gate at the front of the school.
We have set our charges in line with other Island schools and the cost of employing staff to cover the care. Children booked in until 4.00pm but collected after this time will be charged at the higher rate of £8. Any collections after 5.30pm will incur the late pick-up fee.
3 - 4.00pm £4.00 per child
3 - 5.30pm £8.00 per child
4 - 5.30pm £4.00 per child
Late pick-up fee (after 5.30pm) £5 per child every 15 minutes
We provide a range of activities, indoor games and outdoor sports supervised by school staff. A slice of toast will be provided and children will have access to water.
Please note that bookings can be made up until 2.30pm and paid at the time of booking. We are limited on the number of children we have in after-school care and are unable to accept children not booked in via Schoolgateway to ensure the correct staff to child ratio. In the event of a late request on the day, please phone the school office and check we have a place for your child as we may be full. Payment must be made straight after the phone call.
Bookings will open for the following half term on the last Monday before a break.
When collecting your child, please park in the gravel car park and refrain from parking on the semi circle in front of the grass - thank you.
Broadlea Primary School
Accessibility Statement

Broadlea Primary School
After-School Clubs
We offer a range of clubs throughout the year to children from all year groups. Some are run by outside providers, some by teachers and some by support staff. There are some costs associated with the clubs as staff who are not teachers need to be paid for additional hours and outside coaches charge a fee. We endeavour to keep costs to parents/carers as low as possible without impacting on the school budget. The school does not make a profit with after-school provision.
At some times of the year there may be more clubs on offer than at other times, or more clubs for one key stage than the other. We try to balance everything as fairly as possible but are aware that teachers provide these clubs for free, in their own time, and they must offer them at the best time of year to balance their workload. All teachers offer at least one after-school club per year. We are extremely fortunate, and grateful, that many of our staff are very generous with their time and try to provide more.
All after-school clubs start at 3pm and finish at 4pm. Please ensure that your child is collected on time by an adult if they are in year 3 or below.
Please note that car parking is not available on the school site to collect from clubs as there are still staff in school at this time.
We use Schoolgateway for after-school club bookings and payments. To create an account, download the app to your phone and register using the email address and mobile number we hold for you in school. School Gateway will send you a text with your PIN. Login when you are ready to go or contact the school office if you require support.
If you experience any difficulties logging in, it may be because the school does not have your current email address and mobile number. Please call the office and we will update your record on our system.
As clubs go live each half term, we will send a newsletter out with all the necessary information.
Broadlea Primary School
Accessibility Statement

Broadlea Primary School
Berry Hill Childcare
Berry Hill provides childcare for children aged 12 months to 8 years and is located in a purposely-adapted area of Broadlea Primary School. Although it shares the Broadlea facilities, it is a privately registered child care provider and not part of the school.
Children thrive at this well-established, exciting pre-school. They feel safe and secure. Children confidently leave their parents and immediately engage in purposeful play. The inspirational environment focusses on the children. Inviting opportunities, both indoors and outdoors, engage children's interest. (Ofsted July 2022)
Berry Hill benefits greatly from the unique facilities offered at Broadlea, including use of the school hall, field, Early Years environment and Forest School area. The transition between pre-school and Early Years is a strength with children visiting Broadlea many times during the year prior to them beginning school in September.
Berry Hill occupies two former classrooms, now converted into two light, clean and bright playroom areas: the Blueberries Room and the Strawberries Room. Each has its own access to the outside area to allow free flow play whatever the weather.
The private outside area stretches round three sides of the building consisting of paved areas and grassed areas populated with trees; the area is completely fenced and has a secure access system.
Berry Hill has its own secure entrance to the right hand side of the main Broadlea Primary School entrance. Parking is available in Morrison’s car park or side roads.

Living Difference IV is the Agreed Syllabus for Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton. This is the legal document to be followed for the teaching of religious education in Hampshire, Portsmouth, Southampton and Isle of Wight Local Authority schools.
Living Difference IV offers a set of principles for teachers to make their curriculum to ensure religious education is open to the plurality of ways in which people live in our local, national and international communities.
It describes an approach for teaching, seeking to explain the educational value not only of children engaging with new material intellectually, but also of them becoming better able to discern what is desirable for their own lives, and with others, for the world.

Family Liaison Officer
For useful information and help for Parents/Carers, please click here: Parent/Carer Support
Family Liaison Officer
Hi, my name is Christina Bishop and I am the Family Liaison Officer at Broadlea Primary School. My role is to support our families and to provide pastoral support with any issues that you may have supporting your children, either at home or at school.
I can support you to identify strategies which may be helpful, identify when additional outside support may be needed, signpost to other services, and support children in school. I work closely with other members of school staff as well as other agencies and services.
I am always happy to speak with parents. You can contact me via the school reception or you will find me at the school gates most mornings and afternoons. If you wish to discuss personal matters I can arrange a time for you to come in and meet with me privately. I recognise that everyone experiences challenges in life and there are times when additional support can be beneficial. I believe in working with a strengths based approach and I will support you without judgement to try and identify the tools and support you can access to manage and move forward.
If ongoing support is needed for your family we can provide this via the Early Help process which means we would meet regularly, along with any other services and professionals if appropriate, to ensure that you are receiving the support that you need. An Early Help Assessment involves listening to you as a family to find out your needs. A Family Action Plan will be agreed setting out agreed goals, who will be involved in supporting you and what everyone will do.
I am also one of the Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads and I will attend Child in Need and Child Protection meetings held by Children’s Social Care. I attend these meetings to represent the school and will contribute to decision making and planning. Throughout the process, I will aim to support you as a family to understand the expectations of these plans and to achieve the requirements of the plan in place for your family.
I bring a wide range of previous experience and skills to my role, which I hope to be able to use effectively to promote positive outcomes for our families and provide support when needed.
Please come and say hello and don’t hesitate to come and speak to me if you have any worries big or small, I am always happy to listen.
Broadlea Primary School

Broadlea Primary School
School Uniform
Uniform is an important part of a school’s identity. It reinforces who we are as a community and helps enable students to feel pride in their school. It ensures students are not put under any pressure because of the type of clothes they wear and promotes equality. We wear our uniform with pride and thank you for ensuring your children are properly equipped for the school day.
School Uniform Policy
We use Pendle Sports Shop as our official stockist for items featuring our school logo. You will find all of our activewear uniform items on their website, and ordering is a simple process. Please log in and search for our school, or use the links provided on our website.
Children should bring a small school rucksack of a suitable size to hang on school pegs for their Reading Log, reading book, and homework
Uniform List
At Broadlea, we use an ‘active’ school uniform full-time, rather than having separate daily and PE uniforms.
All Year Groups
Pendle activewear shirt with school logo* (not polo shirt or football shirt)
Pendle training top with school logo OR plain, black half-zip training top
Pendle shorts with school logo* OR plain black PE shorts
Pendle tracksuit bottoms with school logo OR plain black tracksuit bottoms (no commercial logos, patterns, or stripes), OR Activewear Leggings (sculpted or fashion leggings are not permitted)
Alternatives: Plain black skort OR plain black cycling shorts worn just above the knee (fashion or sculpted shorts are not permitted)
Footwear: Plain black trainers suitable for all sports (coloured or patterned trainers, Converse-style shoes, or astro boots are not permitted)
Socks: Plain black, white, or grey socks
Outerwear (Optional): Pendle rain jacket with school logo (only for those who wish to purchase a jacket with the school logo)
Note on Base-Layers: Base-layers are not permitted as an alternative to a training top and should not be worn to school.
The school reserves the right to make a judgement on where pupils’ hairstyles or hair colours are inappropriate for the school environment. However, will ensure that any such judgements do not discriminate against any pupil by virtue of their protected characteristics. Each individual pupil’s scenario will be taken into account where any judgements on appropriateness are to be made, and parents will always have the freedom to complain via the school’s Complaints Procedures Policy. Pupils with long hair must have their hair tied back to ensure that this does not impede their vision, cover their face or provide a health and safety risk, particularly during practical lessons such as PE. Broadlea Primary School
Governors
Governors are strategic leaders within schools and have a vital role to play in making sure every child gets the best possible education. The role of the school governor is demanding but very rewarding and is a great way to give back to your local community.
Our Governing Body at Broadlea Primary School is made up of a group of people who are dedicated and committed to do the best they can for the children who attend our school. We work alongside and support the headteacher and staff in all that they do. Regular training sessions are attended to ensure that we have the knowledge to do the best that we can for Broadlea.
Governors are in school on a regular basis; we hold our meetings at various times of the day and evening. We meet with staff and talk to as many children as we can about their experiences in school and the how they have been learning.
The role of the school governor
Governing bodies have a strong focus on three core strategic functions:
Each individual governor is a member of the governing body and all decisions are the joint responsibility of the governing body.
